title: Styles
headline: Styles are one of the leaner areas, and no finding here rests on a feature being unused. Every page of every surface loads one stylesheet of 183 KB (25.8 KB Brotli); compiling the proposed split with the project's own Tailwind gives shoppers a sheet of 130 KB (19.8 KB Brotli: 28% less raw, 22% less on the wire), leaves the admin's as it is, costs no more scan memory than today (204-212 MB against 221-223 MB), and stops admin-only and test-only edits from renaming the shoppers' file. The rest is copies: a launch theme's home page carries an estimated 45 to 71 KB of style text, of which 10.6 to 17.6 KB is one fixed breakpoint sheet repeated per row and 6.6 to 9.5 KB a second copy of the layout's sheets. The completeness check added one thing the report missed and the split depends on: the admin's form, print and editing parts are drawn on public pages with colour roles that have no value there, so the main button on Kaizena Flow's status and illegal-content report pages has no fill (seen in the built HTML). Before opening is the cheap time for the split: no shopper's cache is disturbed and a missed class is found by the team.

clean: Hand-written CSS has almost no dead weight: 93 of 96 class names, 112 of 113 attributes and all 39 keyframes in globals.css, motion.css, admin.css and the two schemes are used by non-test code (the verified report's sample). The exceptions are four alternatives in the admin's own admin.css, under 0.3 KB.

Every block of feature CSS (motion, brands, gallery, lightbox, menu hover, table, modal, header stages) has code that emits its attributes or classes. None is a candidate to retire; that the demo store draws none of them says nothing about use.
Tailwind's scan is cheap since D378: 0.6 s and about 220 MB for 5,931 files. Scanning all of src is not a build cost worth chasing on its own.

The page builder does not style with inline attributes: a store page carries 23-696 bytes of style="". Settings become hashed classes in a part sheet (src/lib/part-css.ts), which keeps owners' CSS able to win (D100). The sheet itself is compact: Meridian's 10 rows are 6.7 KB as one sheet, 1.3 KB gzip, with two @media blocks in all.

Style generation is not paid per request: store pages are prerendered shells revalidated every 15-60 minutes, and the reads behind them are cached ('use cache' in src/server/text-styles.ts:50 and src/server/fonts.ts:159). The builder's canvas recomputes the page's part CSS on each edit in about 5.5 ms for the largest launch theme's home page: under a frame.

Fonts are done well: one stylesheet per family from a cached route, kept for a year, cut to the EU's scripts and the builder's weights (src/app/api/fonts/css/[slug]/route.ts, docs/performance.md:61-62).
The admin's own CSS is already a separate file that only admin pages load (21 KB, 3.5 KB Brotli). Loading both colour schemes costs 0.44 KB Brotli: not worth a second file.
The motion script is loaded only where a page needs it (src/components/motion-support.tsx:10-20).
The dark variant's double writing (by attribute and by the device) is 0.17 KB Brotli, and it is what lets a page be dark without scripts (D99). Leave it.
Theme variables are small and bounded (1.4-1.8 KB per store) and owners' CSS is checked and capped at 50,000 characters a sheet (src/lib/custom-css.ts:19).

Class names kept in stored pages are the themes' own (meridian-hero and the like in src/lib/signature/*.ts), styled by the theme's CSS, not Tailwind utilities; the four migration files hold no class attribute. So no stored content depends on Tailwind's scan, and the split of CS-1 cannot orphan it.
Inline layout-level CSS is the right default at today's sizes: it is paid once per full page load, and an external file would add a render-blocking request to every first visit.

findings.title: Shop pages use admin-only colour roles that have no value outside the admin
findings.evidence: globals.css:62-66 says the roles (bg-card, border-line and the rest) are set only inside the admin. In the built files the global sheet has .border-line{border-color:var(--line)} and .bg-card{background-color:var(--card)} and no definition of --line or --card; the admin's file defines them only under html[data-admin] or [data-scheme-preview]. Counted again by the planner with the role names of globals.css:67-104: 20 uses on 14 lines of seven files outside the admin folders. border-line on the colour and option swatches of combined listings (product-card.tsx:109-110, content-grid.tsx:206, product-parts.tsx:1347-1348); border-line bg-card on one checkout field (checkout-form.tsx:460); the supplier's page (supply/[token]/page.tsx: its field look on line 17, four borders, and text-danger-text on the problem line 60); the product passport (two borders); and the on-site editor's own toolbar (markup-editor.tsx:170: hover:bg-sunken aria-pressed:bg-inverse aria-pressed:text-inverse-ink). The supplier and passport layouts set neither data-admin nor a theme. With the variable unset the declaration is invalid at computed-value time: a border takes the text colour, a background is see-through, an error line is not red. Not looked at in a browser.
findings.cost: No bytes. A wrong border on swatches in every store, one checkout field, the supplier's page and the passport; an error line that does not look like one; a pressed tool that looks unpressed. It also shows what one shared sheet hides: the build cannot tell a shop file that it used an admin class.
findings.who_pays: Shoppers and suppliers, in what they see; the team, when CS-1 is done and these classes must be decided.
fix_steps: 1. Replace the role names with the site's own in the seven files: border-line -> border-border in src/components/product-card.tsx:109-110, src/components/content-grid.tsx:206 (twice), src/components/product-parts.tsx:1347-1348, src/app/passport/[id]/page.tsx:31 and 137, and src/app/supply/[token]/page.tsx:68, 76, 122 and 129.
2. src/components/checkout-form.tsx:460 and the field constant at src/app/supply/[token]/page.tsx:17: 'border-line bg-card' -> 'border-border bg-background'.
3. src/app/supply/[token]/page.tsx:60: text-danger-text -> 'text-red-700 dark:text-red-400', the pair the storefront's own alerts use (rg 'role="alert" className' src/components shows it).

4. src/components/inline-edit/markup-editor.tsx:170: 'hover:bg-sunken aria-pressed:bg-inverse aria-pressed:text-inverse-ink' -> 'hover:bg-surface aria-pressed:bg-foreground aria-pressed:text-background'.

5. New test file src/lib/stylesheet-sources.scan.test.ts (CS-1, CS-6 and CS-9 add to it). First rule: read the role names from the '--color-<role>: var(--<role>)' lines of the @theme block in the site's CSS, then fail for any non-test .ts or .tsx under src/app (outside src/app/admin) or src/components (outside src/components/admin) that names a class ending in one of them behind bg-, text-, border-, ring-, outline-, divide-, fill-, stroke-, accent-, decoration-, from-, via- or to-, with or without variants. Add a would-notice case: the same check on src/components/admin/modal.tsx finds roles.
6. Look at the swatches on a product card and a product page with a combined listing, the checkout field, the supplier's page and a passport, in light and in dark.

findings.title: The admin's form, print and editing parts are drawn on public pages without the colours they read: the main button on Kaizena Flow's status and report pages has no fill
findings.evidence: Eleven files under src/components/admin are drawn by pages outside the admin (import walk from the 644 non-admin files of src/app and src/components, not through src/server): action-form.tsx, admin-text-context.tsx, admin-text.tsx, colour-field.tsx, colour-library.tsx, css-code-editor.tsx, design-cards.tsx, modal.tsx, rich-text-editor.tsx, text-styles.tsx and work/print-button.tsx. They name 13 admin colour roles 125 times (line 41, card 17, brand 14, sunken 13, ink 8, danger-text 8, brand-ink 8, inverse 4, inverse-ink 4, ink-2 3, warning-text 2, edge 2, canvas 1). A role has a value only under html[data-admin] or [data-scheme-preview]; the global sheet has .bg-brand{background-color:var(--brand)} and no --brand. Seen in the build's own output: .next/server/app/status.html and report.html each hold <button type="submit" class="min-h-10 rounded-pill bg-brand px-4 text-sm font-medium text-brand-ink disabled:opacity-40">, their <html> carries data-store-theme and no data-admin, and the one stylesheet they link is the global one. So the main button of the status page's sign-up and of the illegal-content notice form (D411) has a see-through background and the page's text colour. That is SubmitButton's default look (action-form.tsx:152-155), used without a className at status.tsx:58 and 191, report.tsx:90, sign-up-confirm.tsx:66 and get-domain.tsx:43. The component has a className prop for this very case (action-form.tsx:137: 'where the admin's colours are not set', D456) and sign-up passes one; sign-up.html is right. ActionForm's own error list is text-danger-text (line 104) and its success box border-line bg-card (line 43), on the same pages. A store's hosted invoice draws the admin's Print button (hosted-invoice.tsx:61; print-button.tsx:65: bg-brand text-brand-ink). The staff's editing on the live site draws the admin's rich text toolbar (rich-text-inline.tsx:102) and text styles (site-editor.tsx:189): the toolbar's pressed state is bg-inverse text-inverse-ink (rich-text-editor.tsx:126), so a pressed Bold looks like an unpressed one. Inside the admin the mirror mapping already exists: admin.css:20-32 gives the site's names (--background, --border, --accent) the roles' values 'for what draws a store's look'. Not looked at in a browser: the computed style follows from the built CSS and HTML.
findings.cost: No bytes. A main button that does not look like a button on two public pages of Kaizena Flow (one of them a legal notice form), on the confirm and get-domain pages, and on every hosted invoice; errors that are not red; a toolbar whose state cannot be read. It grows with each admin part reused outside the admin, and nothing checks it.
findings.who_pays: Visitors of kaizenaflow.com, a store's invoice customers and staff editing on the live site, in what they see; the team at CS-1.
fix_steps: 1. In the site's CSS (src/app/globals.css today, right after the dark blocks that end at line 170; src/app/_styles/base.css once CS-1 has moved the body) add one block under the selector html:not([data-admin]) that gives each role a page outside the admin can meet the site's own colour: --card and --canvas: var(--background); --sunken: var(--surface); --line and --edge: var(--border); --ink: var(--foreground); --ink-2: var(--muted); --inverse: var(--foreground); --inverse-ink: var(--background); --brand: var(--accent); --brand-ink: var(--accent-foreground); --danger-text: #b91c1c; --warning-text: #b45309. Give the two signal colours their dark values (#f87171, #fbbf24) the way the file writes --background's: once under @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) for html:not([data-admin]):not([data-color-mode="light"]) and once for html:not([data-admin])[data-color-mode="dark"]. The selector cannot match in the admin, so admin.css:20-32 (--background: var(--card)) can never form a loop with it.

2. Rewrite the comment at src/app/globals.css:62-66: outside the admin the roles follow the site's own colours, for the admin's parts a page there draws; shop code still writes the site's names (CS-7's rule).

3. src/components/work/hosted-invoice.tsx:3 and 61: draw DocumentPrintButton from src/components/documents/document-print-button.tsx (same props: label, documentTitle) in place of the admin's PrintButton. The store's own print button then follows the store's theme, and one admin file leaves the shared list (10 left).

4. Optional, for the owner's design (docs/site-design.md): at status.tsx:58 and 191, report.tsx:90, sign-up-confirm.tsx:66 and get-domain.tsx:43 pass className='button-primary min-h-11 px-5 font-medium disabled:opacity-40', as src/components/account-sign-in.tsx:60 does, so the button follows the theme's button shape too. Step 1 alone already gives a filled pill in the accent colour.

5. src/lib/stylesheet-sources.scan.test.ts (from CS-7), second rule: walk value imports (static and import(), type-only skipped, not into src/server) from the non-admin files of src/app and src/components; for every file under src/components/admin or src/app/admin the walk reaches, each role class it names must have a line in the html:not([data-admin]) block. Would-notice case: the walk from src/components/inline-edit/site-editor.tsx reaches src/components/admin/text-styles.tsx.

6. e2e/content-reports.spec.ts, in the test that opens /report (line 34): expect the 'Send the notice' button not to have the computed background-color rgba(0, 0, 0, 0). The same line for the print button in the hosted invoice's spec (rg -l 'hosted|invoice' e2e).
7. Look at /status, /report, the sign-up confirm page, /get-domain, a hosted invoice and the on-site editor with Bold pressed, in light and in dark; send the owner the before and after screenshots.

8. docs/admin-style.md section 4: say that outside the admin the roles follow the site's colours through this one block, and that a new admin part reused outside the admin needs its roles there (the scan test says which).

findings.evidence: The build makes two CSS files: 3-w0shgm-eqtf.css (183,124 B raw, 31,864 gzip, 25,832 Brotli), linked by all 32 sampled pages, and 3jc9lkep25kye.css (21,083 B), linked only by the 16 admin pages. The verified report found 728 of 1,749 utility classes (46.7 KB) named only in the two admin folders and none of them on any of the 16 shop and site samples. The planner compiled the proposed entries with the project's own Tailwind 4.3.3 (compile, oxide scan, lightningcss), outside the repo. The same pipeline on today's globals.css gives 1,750 classes and 181,586 B against the build's 1,749 and 183,124, so it is a fair stand-in. findings.title: The fixed breakpoint sheet is drawn again with every row
findings.evidence: RowView draws <PartStyles rows={[row]}> for each row of a page, header and footer (page-article.tsx:223, reached from site-parts.tsx:345 too), and PartStyles draws BreakpointSheet beside the row's own sheet (part-styles.tsx:41-49 and 57-66). The sheet is 1,760 B and the same text for every store on the default screen sizes. The layout already draws it once through StoreThemeStyles (store-theme.tsx:31); a store's rows use the same sizes as its layout (src/server/breakpoints.ts:12-17 reads the store's theme, as the layout does). React merges equal hrefs in the HTML, but its payload writer gives every string of 1,024 characters or more a row of its own each time (read at the cited line). Counted by the planner: the href kz-bp-j5um1l1cw is 4 times in store-home.html (one row), 3 times on store pages without rows, 2 times on Kaizena Flow's front page. With the real functions on the six launch themes: home pages have 6-10 rows, so 10.6-17.6 KB of per-row copies in the payload, more than the rows' own CSS as one sheet (4.2-6.7 KB). Row sheets also repeat each other: 6.3-12.4 KB one by one against 4.2-6.7 KB together.
findings.cost: 1,760 B of text per row in every document and in every payload answer for a page: navigations and each of the 11 to 50 prefetches a storefront load makes. On the wire it is small (about 0.1-0.3 KB Brotli per document); the cost is text the server serialises, the cache stores and the phone parses for nothing, on every page of every store.
findings.who_pays: A shopper's browser, per page view and per prefetched page; the server, which writes the string per row at each render.
fix_steps: 1. src/components/part-styles.tsx: take <BreakpointSheet> out of StoreSheet (line 45) and out of PartStyles' branch for Kaizena Flow's pages (line 62); PartStyles then draws only the rows' or blocks' own sheet. Export a small async server component PreviewBreakpoints({ owner }) that draws <BreakpointSheet breakpoints={await breakpointsFor(owner)} />.

2. src/components/store-theme.tsx: StoreThemeStyles takes an optional rowSizes (Breakpoints). After the theme's own BreakpointSheet (line 31) it draws a second one for rowSizes only when breakpointClassCss(rowSizes, 'media') differs from the theme's. Pass rowSizes={DEFAULT_BREAKPOINTS} at src/components/platform-root.tsx:72, src/components/docs/docs-root.tsx:37 and src/components/theme-preview-root.tsx:30: rows on Kaizena Flow's pages are drawn at the default sizes (owner null), and this keeps today's output if the theme's sizes ever differ. Store layouts pass nothing.

3. The admin has no layout that draws the sheet, so each place there that draws site rows draws <PreviewBreakpoints owner={the store's id or null} /> once, inside its preview: src/app/admin/(gated)/[store]/pages/drawing.tsx (its two views), src/app/admin/(gated)/(print)/account/templates/kaizen/[templateId]/preview/page.tsx, src/app/admin/(gated)/(print)/platform/site-design/[install]/preview/page.tsx, src/app/admin/(gated)/platform/pages/editor-views.tsx, src/app/admin/account/themes/[presetId]/preview/page.tsx and src/components/admin/install-preview-view.tsx. The builder's canvas has its own (CanvasPartStyles) and is not touched.

A scan test (in src/lib/stylesheet-sources.scan.test.ts or beside part-css's tests): every non-test file under src/app/admin or src/components/admin that imports page-article, article-view, product-parts, site-parts or store-page-article names PreviewBreakpoints; and every root layout outside the admin that can draw rows draws StoreThemeStyles (the three store layouts, PlatformRoot, DocsRoot, ThemePreviewRoot).

In PageArticle (src/components/page-article.tsx:106-132) and SiteRows (src/components/site-parts.tsx:335-349) draw one async sheet for all rows (theme layers read once, then partCss(themedRows(rows), 'site', sizes, 'media')), and tell RowView not to draw its own. findings.title: Layout-level style sheets are carried three times in each store document
findings.evidence: Theme variables, breakpoint classes, text styles, the store's own CSS and the header's and footer's CSS are <style href precedence> elements drawn by the layout (layout.tsx:164-170): inline in every document, once in the HTML and once in the payload. In store documents each is there a third time: the theme sheet's href is 3 times in store-home.html and 2 times in Kaizena Flow's front page. The cause, which the verified report left open, is in Next's source: a root layout with a children slot and one more slot is wrapped in a boundary whose not-found fallback is the layout drawn again (create-component-tree.js:551 and 659-668; its comment says it 'renders the RootLayout twice'). The market layout has the cart drawer's slot (layout.tsx:104). With the real functions: a launch theme's layout-level sheets are 6.6-9.5 KB (theme variables 1.4-1.5 KB, breakpoint sheet 1.8 KB, the theme's own CSS 3.4-6.3 KB), so 20-28 KB per document in three copies.
findings.cost: For a store on a launch theme, 6.6-9.5 KB raw per document for the copy nobody needs (estimate from measured parts); about 0.1-0.3 KB Brotli. Paid on full page loads only: client navigations inside a store do not resend the layout. The ceiling is five sheets of 50,000 characters, each three times.
findings.who_pays: A shopper's browser on every full page load; the CDN and function, which store and send larger documents.
fix_steps: 1. Nothing of its own for the third copy: it goes when the storefront-client plan's SC-8 moves the cart drawer's slot off the root layout (the same finding as PL-2 and PM-1). Do not build a second fix here.

2. Keep the layout-level CSS inline. Write the reason into docs/performance.md (the 'Styles' part of CS-3): an external per-store sheet trades about 2 KB of inline Brotli for one more render-blocking request on a first visit and helps only repeat full loads.

3. Watch it with CS-3's inline-style budget, and add one line to docs/performance.md: look again at an external, hashed, immutable sheet (the href's hash already exists) when real stores' layout-level CSS commonly passes about 10 KB.
4. After SC-8, lower the count in CS-3 step 2 and note the theme sheet's count (2) in docs/performance.md.
tests_and_rules: e2e/performance.spec.ts: CS-3's inline-style budget is the check.
e2e/custom-css.spec.ts and src/lib/theme.test.ts hold what the sheets say; nothing changes for them.
Rule D100 (docs/decisions.md:111): the owner's CSS comes after the theme and wins. Kept: nothing moves.
depends_on: SC-8 (storefront-client plan: the cart drawer's slot leaves the root layout)
findings.done_when: After SC-8, the theme sheet's href (theme-<store id>-) appears 2 times in /s/demo/no's HTML (3 today).
findings.saving: From SC-8, not from this finding: 6.6-9.5 KB raw per document for a launch-theme store (estimate), about 0.1-0.3 KB Brotli. The draft's 20-28 KB raw and 1.5-2.5 KB Brotli assumed an external sheet and a warm cache; on a first visit that saving is zero or negative.
findings.risk: None of its own. The risk of moving the slot is SC-8's.
findings.notes: P3 because it needs no work of its own now: the duplicate is removed by SC-8 and the growth is watched by CS-3. The planner settled the open cause by reading Next's source, which SC-8's plan had already cited. What grows after opening: owners' own CSS and themes; the budget and the 10 KB line say when to look again.

findings.title: A store with no builder motion still downloads motion.css
findings.evidence: In the built sheet the components layer (motion.css) is 18,742 B raw / 4,309 B gzip / 3,815 B Brotli (the planner's own parse). After CS-1 it would be 14% of the site's sheet raw and 19% of its Brotli. The motion script is already loaded only where needed (motion-support.tsx:10-20, motionNeeds()); the CSS is not. Nothing in it is dead. The six launch themes do their motion in their own theme CSS: rg for motion, backgroundMotion, backgroundLayers and gradient in src/lib/signature finds only each theme's reduced-motion query. So a store on a launch theme does not need this file until its owner adds a builder effect. The file is plain CSS (no Tailwind directive, no nesting), so it could be served as it is. Its rules are not only motion: a gradient background's frame and layers (page-parts.tsx:245-256), background layers (background-layers.ts:172-212) and split text need it for structure.
findings.cost: 3.8 KB Brotli (4.3 KB gzip), render-blocking, on the first visit to every store and on every admin screen. A store that uses no builder motion pays the same as one that uses all of it.
fix_steps: 1. Do not build this now. After opening, measure with a read-only script over published pages, headers and footers: the share whose rows need the sheet (motionNeeds(rows).any, or any gradient background, or any background layers). Write the share into docs/performance.md.

2. Only if clearly more than half of real page views would not need it: a prebuild step writes motion.css, minified and beginning with '@layer theme, base, components, utilities;' (so the layer order holds whichever sheet arrives first), to public/ under a name with its content hash, and a generated module exports the address.

3. MotionSupport (src/components/motion-support.tsx) draws <link rel="stylesheet" precedence> to it when the page, header or footer needs it; widen MotionNeeds with a flag for gradient backgrounds and background layers (src/lib/motion-attrs.ts:279-309). The site's entry drops @import "./motion.css"; the admin's entry keeps it for the canvas.

4. Tests: src/lib/motion-css.test.ts:18-20 expects the import in globals.css and must expect the link instead; one new test ties the gate to every attribute motion.css styles (each [data-fx-*] selector of the file has a code path that sets the flag).
tests_and_rules: src/lib/motion-css.test.ts (the catalogue and the sheet are two halves of one thing; line 18 holds the import), src/lib/background-layers.test.ts:51, e2e/motion.spec.ts, e2e/animation.spec.ts.

Rule in src/app/motion.css:7-16: content is always reachable (no scripts, reduced motion, the 4 s failsafe). A sheet that fails to load must leave content visible: the hidden start state lives in that sheet, so it does.

Next's CSS guide (node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/01-getting-started/11-css.md:294): imported CSS follows the importing segment and is not removed on navigation, so this needs a hand-made link, not an import.
depends_on: A measured share of real pages that need motion.css, after opening
findings.done_when: The share of published pages that need motion.css is written in docs/performance.md with the decision; if built, a store page without builder motion links no motion stylesheet and the site's sheet is 18.7 KB raw smaller.
findings.saving: If built and if most pages have no builder motion: 3.8 KB Brotli / 4.3 KB gzip / 18.7 KB raw per first visit. Nothing on pages with motion, which make one more render-blocking request instead.
findings.risk: A page that has data-fx attributes but no sheet shows broken backgrounds (layers fall into the flow); the gate test of step 4 is what stands between. If most real stores add an entrance somewhere, most pages load an extra file and the change is a net loss. How owners will use motion is unknown before opening.
findings.notes: P3: true, but not worth doing now. It needs a build step and a hand-made stylesheet link for 3.8 KB, and its sign depends on use nobody can know before opening. This is not an argument from disuse: the idle cost is real and small, and the plan is to measure before paying for the fix. The draft's 'up to 7.2 KB gzip' is withdrawn (see refuted).
